review_reasons: The change meets the spec: the type and member names match exactly, the routes and status codes match the table, and the 14-day loan, 3-loan limit, rounded-down fee with its 10.00 cap, and the strict `DueOn < now` overdue check are all right. Every time comes from the injected TimeProvider.

It handles a SQLite problem the spec doesn't mention. Value converters mark DateTimes read back from the database as UTC, so the JSON ends in 'Z' and DueOn/ReturnedOn compare correctly. A filtered unique index allows only one active loan per book, and the DbUpdateException catch returns 409 when two borrows race for the same book.

The tests are strong. Each handler has unit tests on in-memory SQLite covering every 404, 409 and 400 path, the edge cases at the due time and the fee cap, and returned loans being excluded. There are also round-trip tests that times come back as UTC, and an end-to-end WebApplicationFactory test that swaps in a fake clock and a temporary database file.

Minor gaps: the 3-loan limit has no protection against concurrent borrows, unlike the book limit. TestDb.Create never disposes the SqliteConnection it opens. The 400 responses have no body explaining the error. The HTTP-level test covers only the happy path.
